name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,333

clue.text: Girl outwardly loving and enchanting

indicators.note: outwardly points to the outside of the word, so only its first and last letters are kept

blocks.note: the two outside letters of the word girl
amorous means feeling or showing love

explanation.surface: A description of a young woman who is affectionate and charming.
explanation.definitionFit: Something glamorous has an alluring, bewitching charm, which is what enchanting describes.

clue.text: Fail to work with inventor? Certainly

blocks.note: a machine that goes is working
Alexander Graham Bell, inventor of the telephone
an informal yes

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a device will fail to work alongside its inventor and gets a confident yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fail to work' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at 'Fail'.
explanation.definitionFit: To go belly up is an idiom for collapsing or going bust, like a dead fish floating upside down.

clue.text: Team magazine

blocks.note: first meaning: the London football club
second meaning: a store of weapons and ammunition

explanation.walkthrough: 'Team magazine' looks like a club's own publication; magazine here is an arms store, not a periodical.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenal is a famous football club in north London, and an arsenal is also a stockpile of weapons, as a military magazine is.

clue.text: Seemingly wise sort in rowing boat heading off

indicators.note: heading off says the front letter is removed from the word it follows

blocks.note: a coracle is a small round Welsh rowing boat

explanation.surface: A sage-looking figure sets off in a small boat.
explanation.definitionFit: An oracle is a person thought to give wise, authoritative pronouncements, hence a seemingly wise sort.

clue.text: Uncovered shop enhanced somewhat

indicators.note: somewhat means a part of, so the letters are a portion of the next words

blocks.note: sits across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A store has been revealed after a modest makeover.
explanation.definitionFit: Open describes something exposed, without a lid or covering.

clue.text: A fool carrying money in dated cave formation

indicators.note: carrying means holding something inside, so the fool's word surrounds the money
in places the whole preceding assembly inside the word for dated

blocks.note: taken as written
a git is a British insult for a fool
M is the abbreviation for money, as in M1 and M3 supply measures
stale means old and past its best

explanation.surface: An idiot with cash is found inside an old-fashioned cave feature.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest here: the money goes inside the fool first, and that whole unit is then placed inside the word for dated, not at its end.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalagmite is the mineral column rising from a cave floor, formed by dripping water.

clue.text: Medic facing no hospital work, as it were, in decline

blocks.note: abbreviation for doctor
O looks like zero, nothing
an operation, the work done in a hospital theatre

explanation.surface: A doctor faces having no hospital work as their career slides downhill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Facing' just puts the medic in front; 'as it were' signals that the hospital work is an operation.
explanation.definitionFit: To droop is to sag or flag, which is to decline in vigour or position.

clue.text: Inspector not tolerating laxity in locality

blocks.note: Detective Inspector
strict means allowing no slackness

explanation.surface: A police officer clamps down on lax behaviour in their neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: DI is a Detective Inspector in the British police.
explanation.definitionFit: A district is an area or region, a locality.

clue.text: Characterising Indian, say, in the main?

definitions.text: Characterising Indian, say, in the main?

blocks.note: surface reading: describing a person from India
setter's reading: the main is the sea, and Indian, say, is one of the great bodies of water, so the word describes it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Indian' looks like a person; it names the Indian body of water, and 'the main' is an old word for the high seas.
explanation.definitionFit: Oceanic means relating to the great seas, so it is the adjective for the Indian and its fellows.

clue.text: Food, for example, stocked by educational body

indicators.note: stocked by says the first item is kept inside the second, like goods on shelves

blocks.note: Parent-Teacher Association
as in 'cities such as Rome', meaning for example

explanation.surface: Food supplies are laid in by a school organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasta is an Italian staple food made from flour and water dough.

clue.text: Blue van's crashed, avoiding very restricted traffic area

indicators.note: a crashed vehicle is smashed up, so its letters are scrambled
avoiding means steering clear of, so that letter is left out

blocks.note: taken as written
V is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: A blue van has crashed while swerving to avoid a closed-off part of the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A bus lane is a strip of road reserved for buses, so other traffic is restricted from it.

clue.text: Swelling muscles two seconds back

indicators.note: back says these letters are read from the end towards the start

blocks.note: abdominal muscles
S and SEC are both abbreviations for second

explanation.surface: Abdominal muscles bulge for a couple of seconds afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An abscess is a pus-filled swelling in body tissue.

clue.text: New driver operating by Fenland location without company

blocks.note: L for learner, the plate on a new driver's car
a machine that is on is working
Ely is a cathedral city in the Fens of Cambridgeshire, England

explanation.surface: A learner driver out on the flat Fenland roads with nobody alongside.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a new driver displays L plates; the Fens are low-lying marshland in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Lonely describes being solitary, without anyone else around for companionship.

clue.text: Tennis player in largely awkward game

indicators.note: largely means most but not all, so the last letter is dropped
game as in a game leg means lame or crippled, so the letters are set awry

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tennis player is caught up in a mostly clumsy match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' looks like the noun for a match, but here it is the adjective meaning lame.
explanation.definitionFit: Stan Wawrinka is a Swiss tennis professional and three-time Grand Slam singles champion.

clue.text: Minor cost possibly probed by unionist in business group

indicators.note: possibly suggests one of several arrangements of these letters
probed means poked into, so the next letter goes inside

blocks.note: taken as written
U is the abbreviation for Unionist, as in Ulster Unionist

explanation.surface: A small expense is scrutinised by a union member within a company group.
explanation.definitionFit: A consortium is an association of companies joined for a common business venture.

clue.text: Variable drink in university

blocks.note: a letter used for an unknown in algebra
a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A varying drinks offering found on a college campus.
explanation.definitionFit: Yale is an Ivy League university in New Haven, Connecticut.

clue.text: It's produced by soldiers in a colony?

definitions.text: It's produced by soldiers in a colony?

blocks.note: surface reading: troops stationed in an overseas imperial possession
setter's reading: soldiers are a caste of ant, and a colony is an ant nest, so this is the chemical ants secrete

explanation.walkthrough: The colony suggests empire and garrisons; in fact it is an ants' nest, whose soldier caste defends it.
explanation.definitionFit: Formic acid takes its name from the Latin for ant and is the irritant ants spray or inject.

clue.text: Chap about 50 put in terror in imaginary world

indicators.note: about means around, so the chap's word goes round the number
put in places the whole preceding piece inside the word for terror

blocks.note: a man is a chap
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
dread is great fear

explanation.surface: A man of about fifty is gripped by fear in a fantasy realm.
explanation.walkthrough: Two insertions nest: the number goes inside the chap, then that unit is put inside the word for terror, just before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreamland is a pleasant fantasy realm existing only in the mind, an imaginary world.

clue.text: Geordie politician accepting dodgy loan? That's illuminating

definitions.note: a cryptic pointer: the answer is a thing that illuminates

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the shuffled word goes inside
dodgy means unsound or crooked, so the letters are not in their proper order

blocks.note: a Geordie comes from Newcastle in the North East of England
taken as written
Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A Newcastle MP is caught taking a shady loan, which is revealing.
explanation.walkthrough: A Geordie is a native of Newcastle upon Tyne, in the North East of England. 'Illuminating' seems to mean revealing a scandal; it means giving light.
explanation.definitionFit: A neon lamp is a gas-discharge light, so it is a thing that illuminates.

clue.text: Bent type prison reformed

indicators.note: reformed means made over into a new shape

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A crooked kind of inmate has been rehabilitated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bent' looks like British slang for corrupt, fitting the prison; it is the noun meaning a natural inclination.
explanation.definitionFit: A bent is a natural leaning or tendency, which is what a propensity is.

clue.text: Displeasure with battery, maybe

blocks.note: first meaning: annoyance or resentment, as in taking it
second meaning: a crime, of which battery is one example

explanation.walkthrough: Battery sounds electrical; here it is the legal term for unlawful physical attack.
explanation.definitionFit: To take offence is to feel displeasure, and battery is a criminal offence of unlawful violence.

clue.text: A companion beginning to exaggerate pain

indicators.note: beginning to picks out just the opening letter of the next word

blocks.note: taken as written
Companion of Honour, a British order
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A friend who starts to overstate how much something hurts.
explanation.walkthrough: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: An ache is a dull continuous pain.

clue.text: By the sound of it, woman with impenetrable intonation

indicators.note: says the words are judged by how they are spoken rather than spelt

blocks.note: Kay is a woman's name, and dense means impenetrable

explanation.surface: A woman's speech pattern sounds thick and hard to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Cadence is the rise and fall of the voice in speech, its intonation.

clue.text: Joking comment, nothing less, in pub

indicators.note: less means minus, so the round letter is taken away
in puts the shortened word inside the drinking place

blocks.note: a note is a brief remark
O looks like zero
a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: Wisecracks, and nothing more than that, swapped down the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joking comment' looks like the whole definition, but 'comment' belongs to the wordplay, and 'nothing less' reads as an idiom for emphasis when it is a subtraction.
explanation.definitionFit: Joking, as a noun for playful teasing talk, is what banter is.

clue.text: Oil facility about to be put by remarkable railway

indicators.note: to be put by says one piece is placed next to the following ones

blocks.note: re means concerning
fine means excellent
abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A planned oil plant is about to be sited beside a striking railway.
explanation.definitionFit: A refinery is an industrial plant where crude oil is processed into fuels.

clue.text: Book in beginning a mechanical creation

indicators.note: in places the first letter inside the following word

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for book
a root is an origin or source

explanation.surface: A book opens with an account of how an automaton came to be.
explanation.definitionFit: A robot is a machine built to carry out tasks, a mechanical creation.

clue.text: Fellow with prestigious award in circle of followers

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow
and means together with
the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: An honoured academic is surrounded by admirers.
explanation.walkthrough: The OM, Order of Merit, is a rare British honour in the monarch's personal gift.
explanation.definitionFit: A fandom is the community of devoted fans of something, a circle of followers.

clue.text: Son overlooked in joint legal document

indicators.note: overlooked means left unnoticed, so that letter is omitted

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
the wrist is a joint of the arm

explanation.surface: A son was passed over in a shared legal paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' seems to describe the document as shared; it is a body joint.
explanation.definitionFit: A writ is a formal written court order, a type of legal document.

clue.text: Asian language and English found in Asian island

indicators.note: found in says one item is located inside the other

blocks.note: abbreviation for English
the Indonesian island

explanation.surface: An Asian tongue and English are both spoken on an Indonesian island.
explanation.definitionFit: Bengali is the language of Bangladesh and West Bengal in India.

clue.text: Corruption shown by a French lawyer in domed building

blocks.note: rot is decay, moral or physical
the French word for a
District Attorney, a US prosecutor

explanation.surface: A French attorney exposes graft inside a domed civic building.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotunda is a round building or room topped by a dome.

clue.text: Fool damaged pewter with no end of haste

indicators.note: end of picks out only the final letter of the next word
with no says that letter is removed
something damaged is knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A clumsy fool dented the pewter by rushing.
explanation.definitionFit: A twerp is an informal word for a silly or annoying person.

clue.text: Rock band hated room for playing

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are moved around freely

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A rock group loathed the venue they were booked to play in.
explanation.definitionFit: Motorhead was the British heavy rock band fronted by Lemmy Kilmister.
